channel.title: Parallax
channel.description: Same event, different vantage points. Geopolitical news compared across Western, Eastern, Middle Eastern and Russian outlets.

item.title: Intensifying fighting between Houthi forces and government-aligned troops causes thousands of people to flee.
item.description: Escalating fighting between Houthi forces and government-aligned troops in the Marib and Taiz provinces has displaced between 82,000 and 86,000 civilians. While all sources confirm the massive humanitarian crisis and the scale of the displacement, reporting varies significantly in focus. Middle Eastern outlets emphasize the immediate humanitarian consequences and local territorial struggles, whereas Russian sources frame the conflict through the lens of broader geopolitical implications and the roles of external state sponsors.

item.title: Donald Trump calls on Ukrainian President Zelenskyy to stop striking Russian oil refineries
item.description: On September 14, 2026, President Donald Trump called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop striking Russian oil refineries to stabilize global fuel markets. While all sources confirm the link between Ukrainian strikes and rising oil prices, reporting differs on the primary narrative. Western outlets frame the issue as a matter of global economic stability and international cooperation, whereas Russian outlets emphasize the direct consequences of Ukrainian aggression on domestic and international supply chains.

item.title: Oman postpones planned talks between Gulf states and Iran regarding the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Oman officially postponed a high-stakes summit in Salalah involving Gulf states and Iran regarding the security of the Strait of Hormuz. Western outlets frame the delay as a test of regional cooperation and the viability of independent diplomacy without direct U.S. involvement. Conversely, Middle Eastern sources frame the postponement as a tactical pause to build consensus following a recent attack on an Iranian cargo vessel. Both regions agree on the postponement but differ on the primary motivations.

item.title: Iran and United Arab Emirates hold first summit talks to discuss regional de-escalation and relations.
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and UAE Crown Prince Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan held their first high-level talks during the BRICS summit to discuss regional de-escalation and cooperation. While both regions report the meeting occurred, Middle Eastern outlets emphasize the urgency of the dialogue as a direct response to immediate regional volatility. These sources also highlight a fractured regional consensus by noting that Bahrain declined to meet with the Iranian leader.
